signature.name: Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque
signature.detail: Beirut's most recognizable landmark, with its blue domes and tall minarets dominating Martyrs' Square. It is a must-see for its scale and central location. Dress modestly and remove shoes before entering; visit outside prayer times.

signature.name: Pigeon Rocks
signature.detail: Dramatic natural rock arches rising from the sea, best viewed from the Corniche. A classic Beirut photo spot and a pleasant walk. Go at sunset for the best light; the area is free and open.

signature.name: National Museum of Beirut
signature.detail: Houses an excellent collection of archaeological treasures spanning millennia. Essential for understanding Lebanon's history. Check opening hours (usually closed Mondays); tickets are affordable.

signature.name: Jeita Grotto
signature.detail: A stunning cave system with vast chambers and underground river, a short drive from Beirut. A top natural attraction. Boats operate in the lower grotto; photography is restricted inside.

signature.name: Byblos Citadel
signature.detail: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities, with a crusader castle and Roman ruins. A rewarding day trip from Beirut. Wear comfortable shoes for the uneven site; allow half a day.

signature.name: Beit Beirut
signature.detail: A moving museum of modern history housed in a bullet-scarred building on the Green Line. Offers insight into the civil war. Check opening days; entry is often free or by donation.

signature.name: Sursock Museum
signature.detail: A beautiful villa showcasing Lebanese and regional modern art. The building itself is a gem. Closed Mondays; combine with a walk in the nearby Sursock district.

signature.name: Our Lady of Lebanon
signature.detail: A major Christian pilgrimage site with a towering statue overlooking the bay of Jounieh. Worth the trip for the views and spiritual atmosphere. Take the cable car up for a scenic ride.

signature.name: Beiteddine Palace
signature.detail: A magnificent 19th-century palace in the Chouf mountains, known for its architecture and gardens. A cultural highlight. Combine with a visit to Deir el Qamar; check for festival schedules.
